AbstractText.Label: Background
AbstractText.content: Treatment for chronic low back pain (LBP) includes different forms of exercises, that to date, have resulted in only small to moderate treatment effects. To enhance the treatment effects, different classification systems have been developed to classify people with LBP into more homogenous subgroups leading to specific treatments for each subgroup.

AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: To compare the efficacy of a treatment based on the Movement System Impairment (MSI) model with a treatment consisting of symptom-guided stretching and strengthening exercises in people with chronic LBP.

AbstractText.Label: Design
AbstractText.content: The study was a two-arm, prospectively registered, randomized controlled trial with a blinded assessor.

AbstractText.Label: Setting
AbstractText.content: The study setting was a university physical therapy clinic in Brazil.

AbstractText.Label: Patients
AbstractText.content: A total of 148 participants with chronic LBP participated in the study.

AbstractText.Label: Interventions
AbstractText.content: Participants were randomly allocated to an 8-week treatment of either treatment based on the MSI-based classification system or symptom-guided stretching and strengthening exercises.

AbstractText.Label: Measurements
AbstractText.content: Measures of pain intensity, disability and global impression of recovery were obtained by a blinded assessor at baseline and at follow-up appointments at two, four and six months after randomization.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: There were no significant between-group differences for the primary outcomes of pain intensity at two months (mean difference = 0.05, 95% CI = -0.90 to 0.80) and disability at two months (mean difference = 0.00, 95% CI = -1.55 to 1.56). There also were no statistically significant differences between treatment groups for any of the secondary outcome measures.

AbstractText.Label: Limitations
AbstractText.content: Participants and physical therapists were not blinded.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: People with chronic LBP had similar improvements in pain, disability and global impression of recovery with treatment consisting of symptom-guided stretching and strengthening exercises and treatment based on the MSI model.
